description: Community-maintained list of known AI-generated design tells. Each entry represents a pattern that has become statistically dominant in LLM-generated UIs, reducing distinctiveness.

cliches.pattern: Cream/off-white background with warm serif typography
cliches.description: Using #F4F1EA or similar warm off-white as primary background, typically paired with a serif font and terracotta or brick accent near #D97757
Dark near-black (#0A0A0A to #1A1A2E) backgrounds with a single high-chroma accent — electric green, neon cyan, or vivid violet — as the only chromatic element
Hero section gradient running from a mid-blue to a purple, often #6366F1 to #8B5CF6 or #3B82F6 to #7C3AED
Using Tailwind's slate-100 through slate-200 (#F1F5F9, #E2E8F0) as card or section backgrounds, producing a cold, corporate feel
Using stock blue (#3B82F6, #2563EB, #1D4ED8) as the primary brand color with no justification from the product's actual subject matter
Using Inter as the sole or primary typeface with no justification — it's the statistical default of AI-generated UI code
A 6xl/7xl bold hero heading in Inter or Roboto immediately followed by a lighter, smaller subtitle — the exact typographic structure of every SaaS landing page
Defaulting to Roboto or Poppins as a 'neutral' body font — these are the most over-represented fonts in AI-generated code
Immediately below the hero, a 2x2 or 1x4 grid of identical feature cards with icon, bold title, and 1-2 sentence description. Ubiquitous. Indistinguishable.

cliches.pattern: Centered hero with CTA button pair
cliches.description: Full-width centered hero with H1, subtitle paragraph, and exactly two buttons (Primary CTA + secondary 'Learn More') stacked or side-by-side

cliches.pattern: Sticky navbar with logo-left, links-center, CTA-right
cliches.description: The canonical SaaS navbar: logo on the far left, centered nav links, primary CTA button on the far right, always sticky
Repeating content sections that alternate between text-on-left/image-on-right and text-on-right/image-on-left, with no visual variation in rhythm or density
White cards with rounded corners (rounded-lg/xl) and a faint box-shadow (shadow-sm, shadow-md) as the primary container for content — safe, bland, omnipresent

cliches.pattern: Fade-in-up on scroll for every element
cliches.description: Applying the same translateY + opacity animation to every section as it enters the viewport — no variation in timing, direction, or intent
scale(1.05) on every interactive element as the sole hover treatment — the most predictable and uninformative micro-interaction
Hero H1 starting with a single imperative verb: 'Build', 'Create', 'Design', 'Ship', 'Transform' followed by a vague object
Feature card descriptions using the structure 'Our [feature] helps you [vague benefit] so you can [vaguer outcome]'
Taglines formatted as 'Adjective. Adjective. Noun.' or 'Verb — Noun — Adjective' with no specific connection to the product
A section of 3-column testimonial cards each showing a star rating, quote, and avatar — indistinguishable across products

cliches.pattern: Terminal phosphor green on near-black (dev tools default)
cliches.description: Using #39FF14, #00FF41, or similar phosphor/matrix green as the BRAND accent on a near-black background. Common in AI tools, dev tools, and CLIs. The 'hacker aesthetic' is now a statistical default — it signals 'AI-generated developer tool' as reliably as cream-and-serif signals 'AI content startup'. Color-002 blocks the near-black+acid pattern; this entry specifically targets the green variant used as a brand identity, not a data indicator.
example_values: green CTA button on dark bg
cliches.correction_note: Verve v1.0 shipped with this pattern. Corrected in v1.1 after self-critique identified the violation. The phosphor green (#39FF14) is now scoped to data-only contexts (severity badges, pass indicators). Brand accent is editorial amber (#D49020), derived from annotation/markup tools — authentic to the product's subject matter.

cliches.pattern: 'No signup required' as a trust signal in workspace headings
cliches.description: Placing 'No signup required' or 'No account needed' as a subtitle in the workspace or demo section — overused to the point of becoming invisible. Users assume it, not trust it.
example_values: Generate or critique. No signup required.
Try it free — no account needed.
